context:
Goal: stale PRs catch up with main without re-reviewing code that did not change.
Problem (rule): the merge tool counts a merge of main as a fix under a fix check. So every guard PR caught up today (#3111, #2783, #3023) owes round 3 and a net value, though each fix check found the PR's own diff byte-for-byte the same.
Based on (ruling): R9 (your 15:44 CST Nov 10: only a change fixed under a fix check waits for round 3); item 613 (your note: round 3 after an earlier pass was 'long since already established' as not wanted); item 741 a (13:21 CST: a lint-only fix after a round-1 pass skips round 3). None names a merge of main, so this is a different act and needs your word.
Based on (read): `merge --help`: 'a fix after a merge of main also qualifies'.
Departs from: main — any fix check after round 1 on a guard change owes round 3; a exempts a catch-up merge whose own diff is identical.
Meanwhile: runner 10's three round-3 reviewers run, and it follows the tool.
home: step merge-lint-fix-no-round-3; ruling R9; decision hold-unsafe-after-round-3

options.gain: A catch-up costs one fix check.
options.how: If the fix check finds the PR's own diff identical to the reviewed one, the merge of main does not owe round 3. Triage files one merge-tool step, joined to step merge-lint-fix-no-round-3.
options.label: Exempt a catch-up merge whose own diff is unchanged (recommended)
options.lose: A merge that changes behaviour only through main's side gets only the fix check's read.

options.gain: Every moved guard head gets a full round 3.
options.how: Main stays as it is: any fix check after round 1 on a guard change owes round 3 and a net value.
options.label: Keep round 3 for every moved guard head
options.lose: Each catch-up costs a round-3 reviewer and its wait; three guard PRs (#3111, #2783, #3023) already owe one today.

ref: runner 10, 13:29 CST Nov 13, via coordinator 13:30 CST
reply: Withdrawn 13:33 CST: you told runner 10 at 13:29 CST that round 3 no longer occurs, and to fix R9 if it still does. That covers this question, so no pick is needed. Ruling r9 carries your words; lane merge-tool-r9-no-round-3 builds the merge-tool change.

title: When a guard PR only merges main in to catch up and its own diff is unchanged, should it owe round 3?
why: Your rulings cover a lint-only fix, not a merge of main; a merge-tool check changes if a wins.
